newsitem.title: FRANCE: French gvt aims to limit spending rise to inflation.
newsitem.headline: French gvt aims to limit spending rise to inflation.

text.p: The French government is aiming to limit the rise in state running costs next year to the rise in inflation, a source close to the government said on Friday.
All areas of spending would also be re-examined closely to allow the government to limit the budget deficit while also funding new measures designed to meet its priorities of reducing unemployment.

The source said that in letters sent out this week to ministers fixing the framework for the 1998 budget, Prime Minister Lionel Jospin called for savings to be made to provide room to fund priority spending.
Jospin pledged during his election campaign not to increase the level of public spending but to make the fight to reduce France's high unemployment rate a priority.
The state must "spend better so as not to increase the tax burden and make progress in the reduction of public deficits," the source quoted Jospin as saying.
Jospin therefore called on his ministers not to ask for an increase in "running costs of the administration, which will be maintained in current francs at the level of 1997 spending".
He asked them to find savings as a a result of a deep re-examination of the way the state is managed.
This might mean calling into question some commitments made by the previous centre-right government.
Savings must also be made in investment programmes.
"All room for manoeuvre available must be found to finance the new government priorities in terms of jobs," Jospin was quoted as saying.
Ministers have been asked to submit their spending plans to the finance ministry by July 3, which will then make the necessary adjustments and present them to Jospin in the last two weeks of July.
France traditionally fixes the spending side of the budget by the end of July, and decides on the revenue side in August before presenting a budget bill in the autumn.
